llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent: it provides local reference text via a simple shell script and SKILL.md, and does not request credentials, network access, or other unexpected privileges.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (Devops Journey reference) matches the included artifacts: SKILL.md documents local text commands and the shipped scripts implement those commands. There are no unrelated requirements (no cloud creds, no extra binaries).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly states outputs are plain-text heredocs with no external API calls or network access. The script only prints heredoc content, handles a command argument, and prints help/version. It does not read arbitrary files, access environment secrets, or transmit data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec; this is effectively an instruction-only skill with a harmless shell helper. The bundled script is a small static shell file — no downloads, no archive extraction, no package installs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables, credentials, or config paths are declared or used. The script uses positional arguments only; no secret-looking env names or unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked always:true and does not modify agent/system configuration. It is user-invocable only and has no elevated persistence or cross-skill changes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears safe and does what it claims: print local reference documentation. As with any third-party script, inspect the files before executing and run them in a restricted environment if you have concerns. Note: there's a minor quoting issue in the help heredoc (the $VERSION variable is inside a single-quoted heredoc so it won't expand), but this is a functionality bug, not a security issue.
